AboutPage.lead: Front-End Developer, actively in training — I started with plain CSS and JavaScript and am now working my way toward React, Next.js, and TypeScript through real projects. Fluent in both French and English, I work just as comfortably with local clients as with international ones, building clear, conversion-focused websites.
AboutPage.availability: Available for freelance work — Porto-Novo / Remote
AboutPage.storyText: I hold a Bachelor's degree in SIL (Institut Universitaire Les Cours Sonou), and started with plain CSS and vanilla JavaScript before moving, through active training, toward React, Next.js, and TypeScript — building real projects at every step rather than stopping at theory. Alongside that, I run coding-challenge series for French-speaking learners on Facebook and WhatsApp — a way to stay sharp on the fundamentals while helping others grow. I'm actively continuing this training (internships, online courses) to strengthen these skills, always with the same goal: clear websites that genuinely speak to your customers.

item1.question: How are your rates set?
item1.answer: Every project is different, so there's no fixed price list: after an initial chat to understand your needs (number of pages, features, custom design or not), I send a clear quote before starting — no surprises along the way.

item2.question: How long does a project take?
item2.answer: It depends on the scope: a simple showcase site is usually quicker to deliver than an application with a back-end or custom business logic. I give an estimated timeline with the quote, and keep you posted if anything shifts the schedule.

item3.question: What technologies do you use?
item3.answer: Mainly React and Next.js (TypeScript) on the front-end, with close attention to performance, accessibility, and SEO. Depending on the project, I also work in more specific requirements — feel free to tell me about your technical constraints.

item4.question: Do you work with remote clients?
item4.answer: Yes — based in Porto-Novo (Benin), I work with both local and remote clients, in French or English. Coordination happens over WhatsApp, email, or a call, whatever suits you best.

item5.question: Do you offer support after launch?
item5.answer: Yes, I stay available after delivery for adjustments or questions — we figure out the details together depending on the project.

hamuz.context: HAMUZ is a Beninese luxury brand in its pre-launch phase. The main challenge was giving the brand an immediately premium feel, even before the official opening, to convert visitors into private-list signups.
hamuz.technicalChoices: Built with Next.js and TypeScript for reliable code and strong SEO from launch. Tailwind CSS made it possible to iterate quickly on a polished design, with particular attention to animations to reinforce the quality expected of a luxury brand.

iphone.context: This project was originally commissioned by a client active in iPhone reselling in Cotonou. The client dropped the project midway — I took it over myself to turn it into a full technical showcase rather than leaving it unfinished.
iphone.technicalChoices: The old React version was fully rebuilt in Next.js and TypeScript. The design was rethought around two trust levers identified with the client before they left: device testing and guarantees, and direct WhatsApp access to an advisor to reduce friction in the buying process.

madatours.context: MadaTours was entrusted to me by my mentor: a tourism discovery platform for Madagascar, aimed at both local and international audiences.
madatours.technicalChoices: Built with Next.js and TypeScript, with next-intl handling three languages (French, English, Malagasy) from the project's architecture rather than bolted on afterward. Particular attention was paid to SEO — per-page metadata, sitemap, auto-generated share image — so the platform would be discoverable from launch.

ecole.context: Site built for a bilingual school in Porto-Novo, aimed at giving families all the information they need to enroll without having to contact school staff for every question.
ecole.technicalChoices: Originally built with React, then migrated to Next.js and TypeScript for better performance and SEO — the same approach used for the Max iPhone redesign. Particular attention was paid to content clarity (programs, teaching philosophy, results) and to the mobile experience, the main channel families use to browse the site.

edudine.context: The same school was managing enrollments, payments, and administrative tracking by hand. Edudine was built to centralize this data in a single tool.
edudine.technicalChoices: Desktop application built in C# (WinForms), with a SQL Server database to store enrollment, payment, and school-year data, plus a dashboard to track their evolution over time.
